doc.title: Rashied Ali and Henry Grimes interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 30, 2009

title: October Revolution and the JCOA distribution
summary: Ali names Bill Dixon, Cecil Taylor and the Bleys behind the October Revolution and the JCOA record distributor.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Was that something like with the October Revolution?
That was one of the beginnings of it.

That was one of the beginnings of it, you know, like Cecil Taylor and Bill Dixon and because I was playing with Bill Dixon at that time. And Cecil Taylor, Bill Dixon and Carla Bley and Paul Bley, and different people like that. They started that October Revolution, actually Bill Dixon was one of the main things in that. And then they got the JOC thing too, which started a record distributing company and so that encouraged people to make their own records and JVC, uh, not JVC, JCOA.

Composers Orchestra Guild. And they got a distributor thing going on and they would distribute our records if we made them and get them to them. It was LPs at that time. And they would distribute it for us, and they had a pretty good, wide range of distributing, and they would get them all over America to different record companies and so we sort of got a little bit of play behind that. And got a little independent too as well. So we sort of got jobs, you know. They started reaching out and getting us on some of us on these jobs. I think that’s really how it got started. It was sort of like we sort of were like competition, especially in New York City. You figure if you come to New York then you have to deal with the jazz musician festivals and have to deal with avant garde jazz musicians. And that’s sort of helped the situation out a little bit.
